title: Google assembles $150B financing program to supply Anthropic with Broadcom TPUs
subtitle: The August 4 arrangement stretches from chip fabrication to data-centre construction, pulls in Apollo, Blackstone, and Morgan Stanley, and gives Anthropic access to 3.5 gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity starting in 2027.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic, Google, and Broadcom announced an expanded compute partnership on August 4 that gives Anthropic access to roughly 3.5 gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity, coming online starting in 2027. The compute will be sited primarily in the United States. The arrangement sits inside a larger Google-led infrastructure financing programme reported by Ground News at more than $150 billion — one of the biggest single-company build-outs ever attempted — pulling in Broadcom for chip supply, Apollo and Blackstone for private credit, Morgan Stanley for underwriting, and a group of crypto miners with existing power-connected sites for data-centre space. This layers on top of the $46 billion long-term Google-Broadcom TPU contract disclosed in April and Anthropic's own November 2025 pledge to invest $50 billion in domestic compute.

The mechanism matters. Broadcom-designed, Google-branded TPUs are not general-purpose chips like Nvidia's GPUs — they are custom silicon tuned for the matrix math of one customer's workload, which delivers better performance per watt at scale but only if you commit to volume years in advance. That is what the 3.5 gigawatts represents: Anthropic locking in the right to specific chips from specific fabs at specific dates through 2031. The private-credit and crypto-miner tranches are what make the timeline believable. Public markets and utility-scale grid interconnects cannot move fast enough for a 2027 delivery, so the financing routed around both.

The broader picture is a bifurcation of the AI infrastructure market. On one side, OpenAI is anchored to Microsoft Azure and, increasingly, Oracle-hosted Nvidia GB300 clusters. On the other, Anthropic is anchored to Google Cloud and its custom TPU stack. Meta and Amazon are building their own accelerators (MTIA and Trainium). What is disappearing is the middle option — the multi-cloud, GPU-agnostic AI lab. The economics of custom silicon at gigawatt scale demand exclusivity, and every frontier lab is now choosing a side. Anthropic's run-rate revenue, which crossed $30 billion earlier this spring and $47 billion by May, gives it the cash flow to make a commitment of this size credible to the underwriters.

For learners: when you read that a lab has "signed a compute deal," the interesting question is not the dollar figure but the fab allocation and the delivery date. Chip capacity is a physical constraint — TSMC's 3nm and 2nm lines are booked years ahead, and a gigawatt of installed compute translates to a specific number of wafers and a specific spot in the queue. If you want to understand which AI lab will still be at the frontier in 2028, look at who has signed multi-year, gigawatt-scale silicon contracts today. Compute pre-orders are the leading indicator; model releases are the lagging one.
